definitions.explanation: A person who saw or heard something relevant, especially in a legal context, or someone who attests to the truth of a document or event.

examples.japanese: {証人|しょうにん}として{出廷|しゅってい}する。
examples.english: To appear in court as a witness.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}の{証人|しょうにん}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: We are looking for witnesses to the accident.

examples.japanese: {結婚届|けっこんとどけ}には{二人|ふたり}の{証人|しょうにん}の{署名|しょめい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: A marriage registration requires the signatures of two witnesses.

notes: Not to be confused with the homophones {商人|しょうにん} (merchant) or {承認|しょうにん} (approval). Common collocations include {証人|しょうにん}{喚問|かんもん} (summoning a witness), {証人|しょうにん}{尋問|じんもん} (examination of a witness), and {目撃|もくげき}{証人|しょうにん} (eyewitness). In legal proceedings, {証人|しょうにん} refers to someone who testifies, while {証拠|しょうこ} refers to physical evidence.
